item.title: Databases
item.description:
On this page, you can find how to create, edit, upgrade and delete Databases in the Cloud Console.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
    • Databases page

    • High Availability

The Database-as-a-Service feature in the Cloud Console is currently in beta. It has not been fully tested across all use cases. Customer support is available for any questions or issues you may encounter.

item.title: Database's Custom Options
item.description:
On this page, you can find what database’s Custom Options are and how to manage them in the Cloud Console.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
  • Introduction
  • Edit Database’s Custom Options
    • PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB
    • MySQL
    • MariaDB
    • Redis
    • MongoDB

Introduction

Database’s Custom Options are a feature provided to modify options of your database. You can edit settings such as connection limits, timeouts, logging and SQL behaviour, depending on the database type. Memory, storage, replication and high-availability settings are sized and managed by the platform for your plan and are not listed.

item.title: Database's Replicas
item.description:
On this page, you can find what database’s Replicas are and how to create and manage them in the Cloud Console.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
    • Introduction
    • Create and delete Replica

Introduction

Database’s Replicas ensure the security of your data: a Replica is a separate Database in another Project that follows the primary Database. You can create up to 5 Replicas of a Database in different Projects of the same region as the primary Database.

item.title: Database's Backups
item.description:
On this page, you can find what database’s Backups are, how to connect backup storage, create and schedule backups and restore a Database from a backup in the Cloud Console.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
    • Introduction
    • Backup storage
    • Automatic backups
    • Create backup
    • Restore Database from backup
    • Undo the last restore

Introduction

Database’s Backups keep a copy of your data in your own S3 storage, which makes it safer than Replicas. You can back up at any time or on a schedule. Everything is on the BACKUPS TAB of the Database details page (there is no separate scheduler tab). Backups need connected backup storage first.

item.title: Database Management
item.description:
On this page, you can find how to create and delete databases within your main database instance in the Cloud Console, and how to manage extensions of PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB databases.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
    • Databases tab
    • Extensions and Settings

Databases tab

The DATABASES TAB of the Database details page lists the databases inside your instance (it is not shown for Redis, which has no named databases). Columns: Name; Charset and Collation (PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, MySQL and MariaDB only); Extensions and Settings (PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB only); Notes - shown only when something was not applied, with the reason.

item.title: User Management
item.description:
On this page, you can find how to manage database users in the Cloud Console: create and delete users, assign permissions and reset passwords.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
    • Users tab
    • Users managed inside the database

Users tab

The USERS TAB of the Database details page lists the users with their permissions in the format database:level, where the level is R (Read) or RW (Read/Write). The main Database user (set when the Database was created) has its own password reset: the Reset password icon on the details page, see Databases.

item.title: Database's Network
item.description:
On this page, you can find what database’s endpoints (load balancers) are and how to manage them in the Cloud Console.

Table of contents

  • Table of contents
    • Introduction
    • Public load balancer
    • Internal load balancers
    • Connection pooler endpoints

Introduction

A Database is reachable through load balancers - endpoints with their own IP address and port:

  • the public load balancer has a public IP address, is reachable from the internet and is restricted by a list of allowed addresses;
  • internal load balancers have an address in one of your private subnets and are reachable only from that network. A Database can have up to 16 of them, each in its own subnet and with its own list of allowed addresses.

Both are managed on the NETWORK TAB of the Database details page. The buttons are not available while the Database is being updated. If a change cannot be applied, the details page shows the notice Load balancer not applied with the reason.
